correctness.rationale: Exact Planck factorization and two positive contrast differences give the strictly decreasing bijection R=F_s(t), whose root is uniquely t>s. Affine inversion then gives all physical parameters and an if-and-only-if realizability region; strict interior continuity constructs an open two-band nonidentifiable family. Exact rational and sampled computational checks supplement, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected accessible primary research and indexed published claims: original forward contamination equations and numerical retrieval are distinct from the asserted exact global identification/feasibility criterion. Rosich et al. (2020) already articulate a three-band possibility for rotational stellar photometric activity, but neither their observational model nor their stated conclusions imply the exact three single-epoch transit-depth inversion and feasibility inequality. The closest prior internal claims are a Planck spectral pivot and a known-contrast multi-epoch identification result with different hypotheses. No source inspected so far entails the full three-monochromatic-channel classification; a general uninspected result remains possible.
residual_risks: A more general uninspected global identifiability theorem for finite mixtures of Planck spectra could subsume the result.
Some historical broadband-activity inverse literature was accessible only in summaries; these were not used as definitive noncoverage evidence.
No claim of independent historical priority or external mathematical certification.

The general three-band identifiability intuition was already described by Rosich et al. (2020); originality is limited to the exact single-epoch transit-depth model, global inverse and feasibility boundaries.

value.rationale: Stellar-transit-light-source contamination is a documented observational inference gap. Three specifically chosen monochromatic bands provide a complete globally identifiable inverse, exact data compatibility check and sharp two-band impossibility; this separates model structural limitations from instrumental noise, while explicitly not claiming practical broadband retrieval.
